title: Find out whether a lane's force push of its own branch was a lease form the guard allows or a bare force it missed
why: Lane habit-is-not-a-guard force-pushed its own branch once on PR #2881; destructive git is refused in shared trees.
source: Coordinator 20:21 CST Nov 13, from runner 10's relay of the lane's own report; the exact command is unread. Triage read hooks/guard.py header lines 114-116 and the force-push block at about line 4709 in a local checkout that may be behind main.
note: Filed 20:22 CST Nov 13. Present guard behaviour (read, lines 114-116 of hooks/guard.py, rule force-push, decision stale-safe-force-push): a push with a lease and --force-if-includes passes; --force or a + refspec refuses; a push that reaches the default branch asks. So if the lane used a lease with --force-if-includes on its own branch (to move PR #2881, head b1d75b152e62, back to the reviewed head), the guard let it through by design (page answers lease-push-own-branch and related); if it used a bare --force or +refspec and it passed, that is a guard hole. Unmeasured which. Next: read the lane's exact command (ask lane session_013NEJL4HbEaurThYorsKFGD, or its events), then replay it through push_verdict. A hole gets a guard step with a test-author red case first; a lease form needs no step. Related: lease-push-refused, lease-push-c-and-d, branch-force-other-worktree.
